! Tschuprow's ''T''
|}

In [[statistics]], '''Tschuprow's ''T''''' is a measure of [[Association (statistics)|association]] between two [[Nominal data#Nominal scale|nominal variables]], giving a value between 0 and 1 (inclusive). It is closely related to [[Cramér's V]], coinciding with it for square [[contingency tables]].
It was published by [[Alexander Alexandrovich Chuprov|Alexander Tschuprow]] (alternative spelling: Chuprov) in 1939.<ref>Tschuprow, A. A. (1939) ''Principles of the Mathematical Theory of Correlation''; translated by M. Kantorowitsch. W. Hodge & Co.</ref>

==Definition==
For an ''r''&nbsp;×&nbsp;''c'' contingency table with ''r'' rows and ''c'' columns, let <math>\pi_{ij}</math> be the proportion of the population in cell <math>(i,j)</math> and let
:<math>\pi_{i+}=\sum_{j=1}^c\pi_{ij}</math> and <math>\pi_{+j}=\sum_{i=1}^r\pi_{ij}.</math>

Then the [[mean square contingency]] is given as

: <math> \phi^2 = \sum_{i=1}^r\sum_{j=1}^c\frac{(\pi_{ij}-\pi_{i+}\pi_{+j})^2}{\pi_{i+}\pi_{+j}} ,</math>

and Tschuprow's ''T'' as

: <math>T = \sqrt{\frac{\phi^2}{\sqrt{(r-1)(c-1)}}} .</math>

===Properties===

''T'' equals zero if and only if independence holds in the table, i.e., if and only if <math>\pi_{ij}=\pi_{i+}\pi_{+j}</math>. ''T'' equals one if and only there is perfect dependence in the table, i.e., if and only if for each ''i'' there is only one ''j'' such that <math>\pi_{ij}>0</math> and vice versa. Hence, it can only equal 1 for square tables. In this it differs from [[Cramér's V]], which can be equal to 1 for any rectangular table.

===Estimation===

If we have a multinomial sample of size ''n'', the usual way to estimate ''T'' from the data is via the formula

: <math>\hat T = \sqrt{ \frac{\sum_{i=1}^r\sum_{j=1}^c\frac{(p_{ij}-p_{i+}p_{+j})^2}{p_{i+}p_{+j}}}{\sqrt{(r-1)(c-1)}} } ,</math>

where <math>p_{ij}=n_{ij}/n</math> is the proportion of the sample in cell <math>(i,j)</math>. This is the [[empirical value]] of ''T''. With <math>\chi^2</math> the [[Pearson's chi-squared test|Pearson chi-square statistic]], this formula can also be written as

: <math>\hat T = \sqrt{ \frac{\chi^2/n}{\sqrt{(r-1)(c-1)}} } .</math>
